"You're late. It's nine."
"Traffic on the flyover. I sent you a message at quarter past eight, did it go?"
"It did. I just..."
"You wanted to check. It's okay, Aditi."
"Where were you before that?"
"Second interview, at the logistics company. Here, the email. And I stopped at the pharmacy for your Amma's tablets. Receipt's in the bag."
"Tejas, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to cross-examine you."
"You're not. Five months ago I let you believe I was going to work every day when I'd lost my job. For three months. You're allowed to ask."
"It's just tiring. For both of us."
"I know. But I'd rather you ask than wonder."
"...The electricity bill?"
"Paid on Tuesday. Screenshot in the family group."
Aditi laughed despite herself. "You're annoyingly organised now."
"I'm trying to be reliable, not organised. I'll keep at it however long it takes."

qa.q: What did Tejas stop at the pharmacy for?
qa.a: Tejas stopped for Aditi's Amma's tablets.

qa.q: What does Tejas's patience with Aditi's questions show about what Tejas wants?
qa.a: It shows Tejas wants to rebuild trust by being open and reliable, accepting that her checking comes from the lie rather than resenting it.

qa.q: Which small acts help rebuild trust in this scene?
qa.a: Messaging when late, showing the interview email, keeping the receipt and paying the bill on time are reliable acts that let Aditi see change for herself.

qa.q: How does Aditi seem to feel about checking on Tejas?
qa.a: Aditi feels tired and a little guilty about questioning Tejas, yet her laugh suggests the trust is slowly coming back.

grounding: Months after hiding a job loss, Tejas rebuilds trust through small reliable acts and open answers, accepting Aditi's checking without rushing her.

passage:
Last spring I told Gurleen I hadn't shared her news with anyone. I had told two people. She found out within a week.
I thought a good apology would fix it. It didn't. So I stopped talking and tried to be someone she could check.
For months I did small, boring things. I turned up when I said I would, even for five-minute errands. If I'd been with our old college group, I mentioned it before she could wonder. When she asked who I'd been talking to, I just told her, even when it felt like being questioned.
Some weeks she still asked twice. Some days it stung. Once I nearly said, "Isn't it time you got over this?" I stopped myself, because I knew that would be me asking for trust instead of earning it.
In November she told me something private again. Small, but real.
I didn't tell anyone.
Eshaan

qa.q: How many people had Eshaan told Gurleen's news to?
qa.a: Eshaan had told two people.

qa.q: Why did Eshaan stop before asking Gurleen to get over it?
qa.a: Eshaan realised that pushing Gurleen to move on would be demanding trust rather than earning it, which would repeat the harm.

qa.q: What was the turning point that showed trust returning?
qa.a: In November Gurleen told Eshaan something private again, a small but real sign that months of reliable behaviour were working.

qa.q: What might those months have been like for Gurleen?
qa.a: Gurleen probably felt a need to keep checking, asking twice some weeks, while slowly testing whether Eshaan's steady behaviour was real.

grounding: After breaking Gurleen's trust, Eshaan shows change through months of small reliable acts and openness, and resists rushing her.

passage:
Counsellor's note, month four: Tarun and Tenzin
Tarun lied to Tenzin for most of last year about where he spent his evenings: he said work, but he was meeting an old girlfriend. When it came out, he wanted Tenzin to "move on" within a week. That didn't work.
Since then things have changed, slowly. Tenzin reports that Tarun now texts when he leaves the office and when he reaches home, without being asked. He shares his calendar. When Tenzin checked his phone twice last month, Tarun said, "Okay," and handed it over, though his jaw was tight.
Today Tarun said, "I still want this to be over faster." Then he caught himself. "But that's me wanting, not Tenzin owing."
What I did next: I told them both that trust is returning in small pieces and that it can't be scheduled. We agreed to meet monthly instead of weekly from now on.

qa.q: What does Tarun now text Tenzin about?
qa.a: When he leaves the office and when he reaches home, without being asked.

qa.q: What does Tarun's tight jaw when handing over the phone suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Tarun felt frustrated or uncomfortable being checked, but chose patience anyway.

qa.q: What is Tarun doing that rebuilds trust?
qa.a: Small reliable acts like texting unasked, sharing the calendar, handing over the phone when asked, and catching himself when he wants to rush.

qa.q: How might Tenzin experience these months?
qa.a: Tenzin is watching for change and still checks sometimes; the steady texts without being asked give slow reasons to trust again.

grounding: Shows a man who broke trust rebuilding it through small reliable acts and openness about his whereabouts, learning not to rush it.

passage:
Tuesday, month five
Opened the bakery at 7 sharp again today. Fifth month without missing once. Parul still checks the shutter time on the camera app most mornings. I saw the notification on the shared phone. It stung a bit.
Then I remembered: for most of last year I told her I opened on time and I didn't. I'd come in at nine and say the till clock was wrong. She has every reason to check.
So I keep doing the small things. I send her the opening photo. I leave the till report on her desk. When she asked last week where I'd been on Thursday afternoon, I told her straight away, dentist, and showed her the slip, without sighing.
Today, for the first time, she said, "You don't need to send the photo tomorrow." I nearly cried into the dough.
I didn't push. I said, "I'll send it anyway, for a bit."
Gurleen

qa.q: What time does Gurleen open the bakery now?
qa.a: At 7 sharp.

qa.q: How did Gurleen feel when Parul said the photo wasn't needed?
qa.a: Gurleen felt moved and relieved, nearly crying into the dough, after five months of steady effort.

qa.q: Why is Gurleen's reply, 'I'll send it anyway, for a bit', wise?
qa.a: It shows patience with Parul's checking and keeps the reliable habit going instead of rushing to claim trust back.

qa.q: What is it like for Parul to still check the shutter time?
qa.a: Parul, who was lied to for most of a year, is watching for proof, and each on-time morning slowly gives her reason to check less.

grounding: Shows a business partner who lied rebuilding trust over months through small reliable acts, openness when asked and patience with checking.

passage: Since the monsoon, Jagdish had kept a small notebook in his shirt pocket. In June his younger brother Omkar had discovered that the evenings Jagdish claimed to be at the mill had been spent at the card games behind the bus stand, and half the money saved for their mother's cataract surgery was gone. Now it was November. Every evening Jagdish wrote where he had been and left the notebook on the shelf. Omkar never said he read it; Jagdish noticed it moved. When Omkar once called the mill supervisor to check on a Tuesday shift, Jagdish felt a flash of hurt, then swallowed it. He had earned that call. He handed over his wages each Friday. He took Amma to her eye check-ups himself. Some nights he wanted to shout, how long will you watch me? He didn't. At Diwali, Omkar quietly asked him to hold the money for the family puja. It was a small thing. Jagdish's hands shook as he took it.

qa.q: Where had Jagdish really spent the evenings he claimed to be at the mill?
qa.a: At the card games behind the bus stand.

qa.q: How did Jagdish feel when Omkar called the supervisor to check?
qa.a: Jagdish felt a flash of hurt but swallowed it, accepting that he had earned the check.

qa.q: Which of Jagdish's habits are rebuilding trust?
qa.a: Writing where he had been every evening, handing over his wages each Friday, taking Amma to her check-ups himself, and being patient with Omkar's checking.

qa.q: What might Omkar's request at Diwali mean?
qa.a: Asking Jagdish to hold the puja money suggests Omkar is starting, cautiously, to trust again after months of steady behaviour.

grounding: Shows a person who broke trust rebuilding it through small reliable acts, openness about whereabouts and patience with checking, without rushing it.
